start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-new-payments-from-a-seller-account with seller_connection service_connection:stripe:example-school and payments_store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_school on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-school-postgres-connection\", \"payments\": \"payment_events\", \"offers\": \"offers\"}, then switch its daily wake on."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the payments are kept in the person's own store, wherever and however that store keeps them, and payments_store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Save the seller's payment account as a service connection (service_connection:stripe:<account>) and the store's login in your vault under a name you choose.

2. Say "Run workflow:keep-new-payments-from-a-seller-account" with seller_connection and payments_store: where the payments are kept, the store's language, the login's vault name, and where in the store the payment events and the offers are.
3. Read what comes back: the since step's newest kept time, the ask step's events, the ids kept and the ids read back. Every id kept must be read back.
4. Switch its daily wake on, so it runs every morning at 6:00 and tells you only when an event was not kept or a step failed.

worked_examples.title: Two new checkouts kept in a school's database
worked_examples.ask: Keep the new payments from my school's payment account in my school database.

payments_store.where: postgresql database example_school on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The since step found the newest kept payment at 2026-09-22T16:26:39Z (created_after_unix 1758558399), and the ask step answered two events: payment-event:checkout:cs_test_sample0001 for offer:example-course and payment-event:checkout:cs_test_sample0002 for offer:example-membership, both from buyer@example.com.
worked_examples.hands_back: kept_ids ["payment-event:checkout:cs_test_sample0001", "payment-event:checkout:cs_test_sample0002"], each written once by its id with its whole attributes object and linked to the buyer row for buyer@example.com; the read-back step found both.
